Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, domain and normalised $\gcd$ monoid.\\% ASK EXPERTS Let $a, b, c \in R$. \\ Let $n \in \N$. \\\\ Then, to prove Fermat's Last Theorem for exponent $n$ in $R$, one can assume, without loss of generality, that $\gcd(a,b,c)=1$.

Let $\Z_9$ be the ring of integers modulo $9$. \\ Let $\Z_3$ be the ring of integers modulo $3$. \\ Let $n \in \Z_9$. \\ Let $\phi : \Z_9 \to \Z_3$ be the canonical ring homomorphism. \\ Let $\phi(n) \neq 0$. \\ \\ Then $n^3=1 \lor n^3=8$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $u \in \cc{O}^\times_K$ be a unit. \\\\ Then $u \in \set{1, -1, \eta, -\eta, \eta^2, -\eta^2}$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $m \in \Z$. \\\\ Then $3 \notdivides \eta - m$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $u \in \cc{O}^\times_K$ be a unit. \\\\ If $\exists m \in \Z$ such that $\lambda^2 \divides u - m$, then $u = 1 \lor u = -1$. \\ This is a special case of the Kummer's Lemma.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\\\ Then the norm of $\lambda$ is $3$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\\\ Then the norm of $\lambda$ is a prime number.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\\\ Then $\lambda \divides 3$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\\\ Then $\lambda$ is prime.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\\\ Then $\lambda \neq 0$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $I$ be the ideal generated by $\lambda$. \\\\ Then $\cc{O}_K / I$ has cardinality $3$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $I$ be the ideal generated by $\lambda$. \\ Let $2 \in \cc{O}_K / I$. \\\\ Then $2 \neq 0$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\\\ Then $\lambda \notdivides 2$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $I$ be the ideal generated by $\lambda$. \\\\ Then $\cc{O}_K / I = \set{0, 1, -1}$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $x \in \cc{O}_K$. \\\\ Then $(\lambda \divides x) \lor (\lambda \divides x-1) \lor (\lambda \divides x+1)$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\\\ Then $\eta^3 = 1$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\\\ Then $\eta$ is a unit.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\\\ Then $\eta^2 + \eta + 1 = 0$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $x \in \cc{O}_K$. \\\\ Then $x^3 - 1 = (x - 1)(x - \eta)(x - \eta^ 2)$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $x \in \cc{O}_K$. \\\\ Then $\lambda \divides x(x - 1)(x - (\eta + 1))$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $x \in \cc{O}_K$. \\\\ If $\lambda\divides x - 1$, then $\lambda^ 4 \divides x^3 - 1$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $x \in \cc{O}_K$. \\\\ If $\lambda \divides x + 1$, then $\lambda^4 \divides x ^ 3 + 1$.

Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $x \in \cc{O}_K$. \\\\ If $\lambda \notdivides x$, then $(\lambda^4 \divides x^3 - 1) \lor (\lambda^4 \divides x^3 + 1)$.
Let $n \in \N$. \\ Let $\left[n \right] \in \Z_9$. \\ Let $3 \notdivides n$. \\ \\ Then $\left[n \right]^3 = 1 \lor \left[n \right]^3 = 8$.

nodes.title: Fermat's Last Theorem for 3: Case 1
nodes.text: Let $a, b, c \in \N$. \\ Let $3 \notdivides abc$. \\\\ Then $a ^ 3 + b ^ 3 \neq c ^ 3$.
Let $a, b, c \in \N$. \\ Let $3 \divides a$ and $3 \divides b$. \\ Let $a ^ 3 + b ^ 3 = c ^ 3$. \\\\ Then $3 \divides \gcd(a,b,c)$.
Let $a, b, c \in \N$. \\ Let $3 \divides a$ and $3 \divides c$. \\ Let $a ^ 3 + b ^ 3 = c ^ 3$. \\\\ Then $3 \divides \gcd(a,b,c)$.
Let $a, b, c \in \N$. \\ Let $3 \divides b$ and $3 \divides c$. \\ Let $a ^ 3 + b ^ 3 = c ^ 3$. \\\\ Then $3 \divides \gcd(a,b,c)$.

To prove \Cref{thm:fermatLastTheoremThree}, it suffices to prove that $$ orall a, b, c \in \Z, 	ext{ if } c 
eq 0 	ext{ and } 3 
otdivides a 	ext{ and } 3 
otdivides b 	ext{ and } 3 \divides c 	ext{ and } \gcd(a,b)=1, 	ext{ then } a^3 + b^3 
eq c^3.$$ Equivalently, $$ orall a, b, c \in \Z, 	ext{ if } c 
eq 0 	ext{ and } 3 
otdivides a 	ext{ and } 3 
otdivides b 	ext{ and } 3 \divides c 	ext{ and } \gcd(a,b)=1, 	ext{ then } a^3 + b^3 
eq c^3$$ implies \Cref{thm:fermatLastTheoremThree}.

nodes.text: Let $S'=(a, b, c, u)$ be a $solution'$. \\\\ The \textit{multiplicity} of $S'$ is the largest $n \in \N$ such that $\lambda^n \divides c$.

nodes.text: Let $S=(a, b, c, u)$ be a $solution$. \\\\ The \textit{multiplicity} of $S$ is the largest $n \in \N$ such that $\lambda^n \divides c$.

nodes.title: Minimal Solution
nodes.text: Let $S=(a, b, c, u)$ be a $solution$. \\\\ We say that $S$ is \textit{minimal} if for all solutions $S_1=(a_1,b_1,c_1,u_1)$, the multiplicity of $S$ is less than or equal to the $multiplicity$ of $S_1$.
Let $S'=(a, b, c, u)$ be a $solution'$. \\\\ Then the multiplicity of $S'$ is finite.
Let $S$ be a $solution$ with multiplicity $n$. \\\\ Then there is a minimal solution $S_1$.

nodes.title: $x,y,z,w$
nodes.text: Let $K = \Q(\zeta_3)$ be the third cyclotomic field. \\ Let $\cc{O}_K = \Z[\zeta_3]$ be the ring of integers of $K$. \\ Let $\cc{O}^\times_K$ be the group of units of $\cc{O}_K$. \\ Let $\zeta_3 \in K$ be any primitive third root of unity. \\ Let $\eta \in \cc{O}_K$ be the element corresponding to $\zeta_3 \in K$. \\ Let $\lambda \in \cc{O}_K$ be such that $\lambda = \eta -1$. \\ Let $S=(a, b, c, u)$ be a $solution$.\\\\ We define $x \in \cc{O}_K$ such that $a + b = \lambda^{3n-2} x$.\\ We define $y \in \cc{O}_K$ such that $a + \eta b = \lambda y$.\\ We define $z \in \cc{O}_K$ such that $a + \eta^2 b = \lambda z$.\\ We define $w \in \cc{O}_K$ such that $c = \lambda^n w$.
